sentiment.label: risk_on
sentiment.reason_it: Il VIX è a 19,92, in calo del 22,31% e appena sotto la soglia di 20, segnale di un mercato meno difensivo. L'S&P 500 guadagna +2,35% e il DXY è stabile a 101,62 (-0,03%). Questi tre indicatori spingono verso un contesto risk‑on, nonostante la guerra tra USA e Iran (articolo 7) che aggiunge un lieve peso bearish. La combinazione di VIX moderato, equity in forte rialzo e dollaro debole rende il sentiment complessivo positivo.
sentiment.reason_en: The VIX sits at 19.92, down 22.31% and just below the 20 threshold, indicating reduced defensive positioning. The S&P 500 is up +2.35% and the DXY is flat at 101.62 (-0.03%). These three data points drive a risk‑on outlook, even though the ongoing US‑Iran war (article 7) adds a modest bearish bias. The mix of a moderate VIX, strong equity gains and a slightly weaker dollar yields an overall positive market sentiment.

market_impact_summary.it: Equity: S&P 500 +2,35% e FTSE MIB +2,69% mostrano un forte slancio risk‑on; Euro STOXX 600 -1,25% resta sotto pressione per la debolezza dei dati macro europei. Fixed Income: TLT +0,05% e US 10Y Yield a 4,86% (+0,10%) indicano tassi ancora alti, ma senza compressione significativa. Commodities: Brent -1,57% (bearish) mentre l'oro sale +0,45% (mixed). Il DXY a 101,62 (-0,03%) è debole, favorendo le valute emergenti e le materie prime.
market_impact_summary.en: Equities: S&P 500 +2.35% and FTSE MIB +2.69% signal strong risk‑on momentum; Euro STOXX 600 -1.25% stays under pressure due to weaker European macro data. Fixed Income: TLT +0.05% and US 10Y Yield at 4.86% (+0.10%) show rates remain high but without clear compression. Commodities: Brent -1.57% (bearish) while gold is up +0.45% (mixed). articles.title: Europe’s Raw Material Future Lies Next Door, If It Does Not Repeat the Past
articles.snippet: Europe often discusses critical raw materials as if geographical distance were the central problem. Lithium comes from South America or Australia. Cobalt comes from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Rare earths are processed in China. The obvious response appears to be finding alternative suppliers elsewhere in the world. But part of Europe’s raw-material future may be much closer. Ukraine and the Western Balkans hold deposits of many materials required for batteries, power grids, wind turbines, electric vehicles, semiconductors and defense…
